summary: Kazuhiro Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Koyasan University around 2000–2004, where he also served as a researcher around 2004.
Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).
Kazumi Yoshizaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University and held an attested post at the National Museum of Ethnology in 2001.

Wasō Harada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities under Esho Mikogami, Hiroo Kashiwagi, Makio Takemura, and Kakushō Ujiie, and held posts at Ryukoku University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Toseiji.

Kazunobu Matsuda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Otani University, he held posts at Otani University, the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kazuo Enoki was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935), served as associate professor there (~1948–1955), and was host at the Toyo Bunko (~1935–1989).

Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Hajime Sakurabe at Otani University, where he earned a PhD and served as associate professor (~1983–2014) and director of the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute.

Kazuo Kano works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg under Katsumi Mimaki, Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and David P. Jackson, and held posts at Hamburg, Kyoto, Koyasan, and Komazawa universities.
Kazuo Matsumura is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1973–1977) and held posts at Tenri University (~1986–1996) and Wako University (~2004).

Kazuo Okabe is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, lectured at Aichi Gakuin University in 1969, and served as associate professor and professor at Komazawa University (1973–2006).

Kazuo Osumi was a scholar of history, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1964) and held posts as associate professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1971–1975) and held a post at Rissho University around 1991.
Kazutoshi Soma is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), where he also held an administrative post, and later served as a fixed-term assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo, founded Shinnyokai, and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle specialized in religious studies, history, and Indology. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago under Mircea Eliade, held posts at Brown and the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study, and was Professor of History at UCLA (~1967–1994).

Kei Kataoka works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, he studied under numerous scholars including Hiroshi Marui. He held posts at Oxford, JSPS, the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University.

Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, was a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (1975), and served as lecturer, associate professor, and professor at Kokugakuin University (1986–1995).
Keiji Iwata was a scholar of religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947) and held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1974–1983) and Otani University (~1986–1993).
